definition: A small, self-supporting stack of grain sheaves, set upright in a field to dry; also, to arrange sheaves in such stacks.
etymology: First recorded in late Middle English, stook has a murky family history: it is probably Germanic, and may be related to words for a stump or upright block. The image is apt—a little cluster of cut grain standing firm in the field.
usage: By late September, the last stooks stood gold and weather-darkened along the hedgerows.
